prompt:
A sharp close-up photograph, camera level with the base, of a machined aluminium exhibition puzzle on a dark bench: a flat base with THREE upright pegs standing on it, marked A (left), B (middle) and C (right), and a small blank engraving plate screwed to the front of the base.

It carries 6 round disks of clearly different widths -- disk 1 (the narrowest) is teal, disk 2 is amber, disk 3 is burnt orange, disk 4 is indigo, disk 5 is violet, disk 6 is dark teal (the widest) -- each with its own size number printed large on its face. The stacking rule is the usual one -- a disk rests either on the base or on a disk wider than itself, never on a narrower one.

All 6 disks start stacked on peg A, widest at the bottom, and are moved to peg C in the FEWEST possible moves (exactly 63 moves), one disk at a time, never a wider disk onto a narrower one. Count the moves of that shortest solution 1, 2, 3, ...

Consider the moment immediately after disk 3 has been set down on a peg for the 5th time in that solution (where it lies at the very start does not count -- only the times it is actually moved). Show the puzzle EXACTLY as it stands at that moment, and engrave on the plate the NUMBER of that move -- one whole number, nothing else. The picture and the engraved number must agree with each other.

Keep the picture clean: no move list, no annotations, no captions. The only characters in the image are the letters on the base and the number printed on each disk (plus the single number on the engraving plate).
